title: UPSC CSE - Indian Economy - Sectors of Economy - Agriculture
subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Which one of the following is the correct description of '100 Million Farmers'?
(a) It is a platform for accelerating the transition towards food and water Systems that are net-zero (carbon), nature-positive and that aims to increase farmer resilience.
(b) It is an international alliance and a network of individuals and farming organisations interested in supporting and Strengthening the development of the organic animal husbandry.
(c) It is a digital platform fully integrated with service providers and built on blockchain that lets buyers, sellers and third parties trade fertilizers quickly and securely.
(d) It is a platform with the mission of encouraging the farmers to form Farmer Product Organisations or Agribusiness Consortiums, thus facilitating the access to global open markets to sell their products.
options: It is a platform for accelerating the transition towards food and water Systems that are net-zero (carbon), nature-positive and that aims to increase farmer resilience.
It is an international alliance and a network of individuals and farming organisations interested in supporting and Strengthening the development of the organic animal husbandry.
It is a digital platform fully integrated with service providers and built on blockchain that lets buyers, sellers and third parties trade fertilizers quickly and securely.

It is a platform with the mission of encouraging the farmers to form Farmer Product Organisations or Agribusiness Consortiums, thus facilitating the access to global open markets to sell their products.
questions.explain:
100 Million Farmers is a platform supporting private and public leaders to position food and farmers as central pillars on the global climate and nature agenda, and accelerate collective action to scale climate and nature friendly agricultural practices.

It has bold objectives for accelerating the transition towards food and water systems that are net-zero, nature-positive, and that increase farmer resilience.

Targeting a fifth of the world's farmer population, the initiative aims to reach one hundred million farmers in order to reach a tipping point that could shape the future of food and water systems.

questions.q: The total fertility rate in an economy is defined as:
options: the number of children born per 1000 People in the Population in a year
the number of children born to couple in their lifetime in a given population
the birth rate minus death rate
the average number of live births a woman would have by the end of her child-bearing age
questions.explain: Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is the average number of children a hypothetical cohort of women would have at the end of their reproductive period if they were subject during their whole lives to the fertility rates of a given period and if they were not subject to mortality. It is expressed as children per woman.

questions.q:
With reference to the sectors of the Indian economy, consider the following pairs:
Economic activity - Sector
1. Storage of agricultural produce - Secondary
2. Dairy farm - Primary
3. Mineral exploration - Tertiary
4. Weaving cloth - Secondary
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Storage of agricultural produce belongs to Tertiary sector. Dairy farming is in Primary sector. Mineral exploration is in Primary sector. Weaving cloth is in Secondary sector. Thus only pairs 2 and 4 are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the concept of 'Small Farmer Large Field'?
options: Resettlement of a large number of people, uprooted from their countries due to war, by giving them a large cultivable land which they cultivate collectively and share the produce
Many marginal farmers in an area organize themselves into groups and synchronize and harmonize selected agricultural operations

Many marginal farmers in an area together make a contract with a corporate body and surrender their land to the corporate body for a fixed term for which the corporate body makes a payment of agreed amount to the farmers

A company extends loans, technical knowledge and material inputs to a number of small farmers in an area so that they produce the agricultural commodity required by the company for its manufacturing process and commercial production
questions.explain: The Small Farmer Large Field concept involves small or marginal farmers in an area organizing themselves into groups to synchronize and harmonize specific agricultural operations. By pooling their resources and coordinating their activities, they can achieve economies of scale, improve productivity, and strengthen their bargaining power.

questions.q:
With reference to WaterCredit', consider the following statements:
1. It puts microfinance tools to work in the water and sanitation sector.
2. It is a global initiative launched under the aegis of the World Health Organization and the World Bank.
3. It aims to enable the poor people to meet their water needs without depending on subsidies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. WaterCredit is an initiative of water.org, not WHO and World Bank. It uses microfinance in the water and sanitation sector and aims to enable poor people to meet their water needs without depending on subsidies.

questions.q:
Find correct statement(s):
1. 36% of India's districts are classified as 'overexploited' or 'critical' by the CGWA.
2. Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) was formed under the Environment (Protection) Act.
3. India has the largest area under groundwater irrigation in the world.
questions.explain: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. CGWA was formed under the Environment (Protection) Act, and India has the world's largest groundwater well equipped irrigation system.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to chemical fertilisers in India, consider the following statements:
1. At present, the retail price of chemical fertilisers is market-driven and not administered by the Government.
2. Ammonia, which is an input of urea, is produced from natural gas.
3. Sulphur, which is a raw material for phosphoric acid fertiliser, is a by-product of oil refineries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The government subsidizes and administers fertilizer prices, so statement 1 is incorrect. Ammonia is produced from natural gas, and sulphur is a by-product of oil refineries used in phosphoric acid fertilizer production.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the case of all cereals, pulses and oilseeds, the procurement at Minimum Support Price (MSP) is unlimited in any State/UT of India.
2. In the case of cereals and pulses, the MSP is fixed in any State/UT at a level to which the market price will never rise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are incorrect. There are limits on procurement under MSP, and MSP is not fixed at a level to which market price will never rise.

questions.q:
Which of the following factors/policies were affecting the price of rice in India in the recent past?
1. Minimum Support Price
2. Government's trading
3. Government's stockpiling
4. Consumer subsidies
questions.explain: All the mentioned factors affect rice prices in India. MSP, government trading and stockpiling, and consumer subsidies all play a role in determining rice prices.

questions.q:
In India, which of the following can be considered as public investment in agriculture?
1. Fixing Minimum Support Price for agricultural produce of all crops.
2. Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies.
3. Social Capital development.
4. Free Electricity supply to farmers.
5. Waiver of agricultural loans by the banking system.
6. Setting up of cold storage facilities by the government.
questions.explain: Public investment in agriculture includes computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, social capital development, and setting up of cold storage facilities by the government. The other options are not considered public investment as they benefit only certain sections of farmers or may be detrimental in the long run.

questions.q: The economic cost of food grains to the Food Corporation of India is Minimum Support Price and bonus (if any) paid to the farmers plus:
options: Procurement incidentals and charges for godowns
questions.explain: The economic cost to FCI includes MSP, bonus (if any), procurement incidentals, and distribution cost. Procurement incidentals are expenses incurred during procurement till the food grains reach the first point of godown.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to organic farming in India, consider the following statements:
1. 'The National Programme for Organic Production' (NPOP) is operated under the guidelines and directions of the Union Ministry of Rural Development.
2. 'The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) functions as the Secretariat for the implementation of NPOP.
3. Sikkim has become India's first fully organic State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. NPOP is implemented by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not Rural Development. APEDA functions as the Secretariat for NPOP implementation, and Sikkim has become India's first fully organic state.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
As per the NSSO 70th Round 'Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households', consider the following statements:
1. Rajasthan has the highest percentage share of agricultural households among its rural households.
2. Out of the total agricultural households in the country, a little over 60 percent belong to OBCs.
3. In Kerala, a little over 60 percent of agricultural households reported to have received maximum income from sources other than agricultural activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Rajasthan had the highest percentage of agricultural households (78.4%) among rural households. In Kerala, about 61% of agricultural households reported maximum income from non-agricultural sources. Statement 2 is incorrect as only about 45% of agricultural households belonged to OBCs, not 60%.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Areca nut
2. Barley
3. Coffee
4. Finger millet
5. Groundnut
6. Sesamum
7. Turmeric
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has announced the Minimum Support Price for which of the above?
questions.explain: Government announces MSP for 22 mandated crops and fair and remunerative price (FRP) for sugarcane. The mandated crops are 14 crops of the kharif season, 6 rabi crops and two other commercial crops. The list includes cereals, pulses, oilseeds, and other crops such as copra, raw jute, and sugarcane.

questions.q: What is/are the advantages/advantages of implementing the 'National Agriculture Market' scheme?
options: It is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities.
It provides the farmers' access to a nationwide market, with prices commensurate with the quality of their produce.
questions.explain: National Agriculture Market is a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities. It facilitates pan-India trade in agriculture commodities, providing better price discovery through a transparent auction process based on the quality of products.

questions.q: Why does the Govt promote the use of 'Neem-coated Urea' in agriculture?
options: Release of Neem oil in the soil increases nitrogen fixation by the soil microorganisms.
Neem coating slows down the rate of dissolution of urea in the soil.
Nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas, is not at all released into atmosphere by crop fields.
It is a combination of a weedicide and a fertilizer for particular crops.
questions.explain: Neem-coating slows down the rate of dissolution of urea in the soil, increasing the availability of nitrogen for crops. It improves uptake of nitrogen, phosphorous and potassium, reduces nitrogen losses, and makes it more difficult for black marketers to divert urea to industrial consumers.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage/advantages of practising drip irrigation?
options: None of the above is an advantage of practising drip irrigation
questions.explain: Drip irrigation can save water and nutrients by allowing water to drip slowly into plant roots. It improves plant growth, controls weeds, and reduces soil erosion. However, it does not reduce soil salinity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Program was launched during 1996-97 to provide loan assistance to poor farmers.
2. The Command Area Development Program was launched in 1974-75 for the development of water-use efficiency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Program was launched in 1996-97 to provide financial assistance to major/medium irrigation projects, not to poor farmers. The Command Area Development Program was launched in 1974 to improve potential irrigation utilization and optimize agricultural production through efficient water management.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the main objective of 'Seed Village Concept'?
options: Encouraging the farmers to use their own farm seeds and discouraging them to buy the seeds from others.
Involving the farmers for training in quality seed production and thereby to make available quality seeds to others at appropriate time and affordable cost.
Earmarking some villages exclusively for the production of certified seeds.
Identifying the entrepreneurs in the village and providing them technology and finance to set up seed companies.
questions.explain: The 'Seed Village concept' involves training a group of farmers to produce seeds of their choice and cater to the needs of themselves and fellow farmers, at appropriate times and affordable costs. It aims to make quality seeds available at the doorsteps of farmers and facilitate the spread of new cultivars.

questions.q: The substitution of steel for wooden ploughs in agricultural production is an example of
questions.explain: The substitution of steel for wooden ploughs is an example of capital-augmenting technological progress. It results in more productive use of existing capital goods, encouraging more steel production and improving overall efficiency in agricultural production.

questions.q: In India, markets in agricultural products are regulated under the
options: Agricultural Produce Market Committee Act enacted by States
Food Products Order, 1956 and Meat and Food Products Order, 1973
questions.explain: Agriculture falls under the State List of the Constitution. Agricultural marketing in most states is regulated by the Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMCs) established by state governments under their respective APMC Acts. These committees regulate the sale of agricultural produce and provide infrastructure for agricultural marketing.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: The Fair and Remunerative Price of Sugarcane is approved by the
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, Ministry of Agriculture
questions.explain: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, on behalf of the government, approves the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane. This pricing is governed by the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. The FRP replaced the concept of Statutory Minimum Price (SMP) in 2009-10.

questions.q:
India has experienced persistent and high food inflation in the recent past. What could be the reasons?
1. Due to gradual switch over to the cultivation of commercial crops, the area under the cultivation of food grains has steadily decreased in the last five years by about 30%.
2. As a consequence of increasing incomes, the consumption patterns of people have undergone a significant change.
3. The food supply chain has structural constraints.
questions.explain: The reasons for persistent and high food inflation include: 1) Increased incomes leading to changed consumption patterns and increased demand for food grains. 2) Structural constraints in the food supply chain, such as lack of warehousing, low farm sorting and grading, and lack of cold chain facilities. The decrease in area under food grain cultivation was around 4-5%, not 30% as stated in the first option.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: With what purpose is the Government of India promoting the concept of Mega Food Parks?
options: To provide good infrastructure facilities for the food processing industry.
To increase the processing of perishable items and reduce wastage.
To provide emerging and eco-friendly food processing technologies to entrepreneurs.
questions.explain: The Mega Food Park Scheme aims to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure for food processing in well-defined agri/horticultural zones. It aims to link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors, and retailers. The scheme focuses on maximizing value addition, minimizing wastage, increasing farmers' income, and creating employment opportunities in rural areas.
